declared: 2026-11-08, before the frozen rustc 1.98.0 oracle of these exact bytes. These shapes reduce census 8's third diagnostic record (core's `const impl Drop for DropGuard<T, F> where F: [const] FnOnce(T)`); their drafts in obj/parallel/census-batch7/repro/g were run through rustc 1.98.0 and this compiler before this declaration, so this is a regression record of that exploration. Each outcome follows the stated rule (every Drop impl bound, binder-scoped or not, must be implied by its nominal type's bounds; a const Drop impl's `[const]` bound is checked as the ordinary bound, and its fields must be const-destructible)

plain-guard.rs.reason: an ordinary Drop impl repeats its struct's paren-sugar bound `F: FnOnce(T)`, which this compiler keeps in a binder scope

core-const-guard.rs.reason: core's DropGuard shape: a const Drop impl's `F: [const] FnOnce(T)` over ManuallyDrop fields is the struct's ordinary bound

higher-ranked-guard.rs.reason: the repeated bound `F: FnOnce(&T)` is higher-ranked over the elided lifetime

added-bound.rs.reason: opponent: the struct has no `F: FnOnce(T)` bound, so the Drop impl adds it (E0367)

stronger-output.rs.reason: opponent: the Drop impl requires `FnOnce(T) -> u8` where the struct requires `FnOnce(T)`, whose output is `()` (E0367)

added-higher-ranked.rs.reason: opponent: the Drop impl adds the higher-ranked `F: FnOnce(&T)` (E0367)

const-field-destruct.rs.reason: opponent: a const Drop impl over plain `T` and `F` fields needs `T: [const] Destruct` (E0367)
